items.t: Banco Bradesco (BOVESPA:BBDC4) Stock Fair Value Edges Lower After Cautious Analyst Revisions
sum: Price targets for Banco Bradesco have shifted, with the fair value estimate moving from about R$22.83 to roughly R$22.25 per share and some individual targets moving from R$21 to R$16. Analysts link these changes to a more cautious tone after the Q3 report and to a higher for longer rate backdrop, with several moving ratings toward neutral and reworking their valuation frameworks. As you read on, you will see how these updated price targets fit into the broader analyst narrative and how to keep track of its next moves.
- Several firms still discuss Banco Bradesco as a core part of Brazil financials coverage, which keeps investor attention on how the stock might respond if macro conditions or rates change over time.
- Itau BBA maintains a R$20 price target, which signals some support for current valuation levels even as it flags a more challenging earnings outlook.

- Citi moved Banco Bradesco to Neutral from Buy and reduced its price target to R$16 from R$21. The bank cites a higher for longer rate backdrop and a need for higher risk premiums, and it now prefers financial companies with more resilient earnings and stronger cash flow profiles.

- JPMorgan downgraded Banco Bradesco to Neutral from Overweight with a price target of R$18, down from R$26. The firm points to challenging trends under Brazil's post election macro setup and expects loan growth to slow as government backed programs and private payroll channels lose momentum.

- Itau BBA cut its rating to Market Perform from Outperform with a R$20 price target. The research highlights a more difficult 2027 earnings outlook following the Q3 report, which feeds into the recent cluster of more cautious ratings on Banco Bradesco.

Brazil Stock Market Today: Petrobras, Itaú And Bradesco Shares Slide After Lula Wins 2026 Election; Brazil Debt And Fiscal Policy In Focus
sum: Brazil Stock Market Today: Brazilian stocks and currency faced selling pressure on Monday, October 26 following the win of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the re-election. He beat right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff. Major Brazilian companies like Petrobras, Itaú Unibanco and Banco Bradesco saw declines in US premarket trading as investors reconsidered the country’s economic future.

The Superior Electoral Court said that Lula received 51.79% of votes while Flávio Bolsonaro got 48.21%. This outcome surprised market predictions of a change in government and a move toward stricter fiscal policies.

Early trading reports showed that US-listed Petrobras shares dropped 22%. Itaú Unibanco and Banco Bradesco were among the banking stocks that fell between 23% and 29%. These numbers are movements and should not be seen as the final closing losses for these companies on Brazil’s B3 exchange.
Reuters also said that November futures, for the real dropped 10% during Asian trading. The Tokyo-listed Nomura NF Ibovespa Link exchange-traded fund, which follows equities fell 15%.
Brazil Election Result 2026: Why Markets Reacted To Lula’s Victory; Ibovespa Falls

Investors had been preparing for a win by Flávio Bolsonaro, who came first in the opening round. Brazilian assets had jumped before the round because people thought a new government might tighten spending.

Before the result Brazilian stocks had finished almost 7 percent higher than they were before the first round. The real had risen 5 percent against the US dollar. Interest‑rate futures also showed that people expected tighter fiscal rules to lower borrowing costs eventually.

sum: Banco Bradesco SA (BBDO) moved up by 8.11%. The Banking & Investment Services sector is up by 0.55%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Bank of America Corp (BAC) up 0.16%; Goldman Sachs Group Inc (GS) up 0.61%; JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM) up 0.20%.

Banco Bradesco ADRs experienced a sharp upward surge accompanied by heightened intraday volatility, primarily driven by major macroeconomic and political developments in Brazil alongside supportive corporate catalysts. The broad rally across Brazilian equities followed the outcome of the country's first-round presidential election, which yielded a stronger-than-expected result for market-friendly candidates. Investors interpreted the election outcome as a positive signal for future economic policy, anticipating potential pro-market fiscal discipline and regulatory stability that directly benefits the domestic financial sector.

As one of Brazil's largest private banking institutions, Banco Bradesco stands as a primary beneficiary of improved investor sentiment toward emerging market financial assets. The prospect of reduced political uncertainty and macro policy tailwinds prompted strong institutional inflows across Brazilian equities and foreign depositary receipts. The market momentum was further amplified by broader foreign exchange movements and sector-wide buying across Latin American banking stocks.

Beyond macroeconomic factors, company-specific developments provided additional buying momentum. The institution recently announced a special dividend, encouraging income-focused investors to position themselves ahead of the upcoming record date. Furthermore, recent institutional filings revealed increased positioning by major asset managers and hedge funds, reinforcing market confidence in the bank's underlying asset quality, growing secured credit portfolios, and resilient insurance operations.

Despite the strong upward trajectory, intraday trading reflected notable volatility. Traders navigated brief periods of profit-taking as short-term market participants reassessed valuations following the initial election rally. Analysts maintain a cautious stance regarding credit growth conditions and leverage, contributing to dynamic price action throughout the trading session.

items.t: HSBC set to grow again in Brazil with focus on wholesale banking
sum: A decade after selling its retail business to Bradesco, global bank expects a much larger local operation

HSBC expects its Brazilian operation to become “many times larger” in the coming years, without returning to retail banking. The expansion will remain focused on wholesale banking, targeting Brazilian companies with international operations as well as multinationals served by the bank’s global network. The arrival of Chinese companies in the country has been one of the drivers of that growth.

That kind of demand has been rising. The number of active Chinese clients served by HSBC Brazil grew more than 21% between December and June. The bank can support Chinese groups interested in buying Brazilian companies using both its local balance sheet and the financial structure of its units abroad.

“Chinese companies are also coming to Brazil. We’ve been able to expand the services we provide to these clients here,” said Alexandre Guião, HSBC Brazil’s CEO, in an interview with Valor. The bank serves these companies in China and seeks to follow them as they expand into other markets, particularly Brazil’s.

One focus is growth in trade finance. In addition, in an acquisition of a Brazilian company by a Chinese group, for example, HSBC can extend credit through units in Asia, Europe, Mexico or other countries where it operates. It can also support Brazilian companies interested in raising funds in Hong Kong or other Asian markets, the executive said.

For Jorge Arce, HSBC’s CEO for Latin America, the region has grown more important for the bank because it occupies an increasingly relevant position in its global clients’ businesses. The shift also reflects the reorganization of supply chains and the search for energy, raw materials and industrial capacity. “For our global clients, Brazil, Mexico and the rest of Latin America are very important. We are where our clients want us to be and where it matters to serve them,” Arce said during a visit to Brazil last week.
HSBC’s international presence also allows it to serve Brazilian companies domestically and follow them into markets such as Hong Kong, the United Kingdom, Mexico and the United States, he said.

Ibovespa Gains as Petrobras and Vale Rally
sum: The Ibovespa edged 0.1% higher to close at 167,927 on Thursday, supported by gains in commodity-related stocks.
Petrobras rose 2.8%, tracking a strong increase in oil futures, which also boosted PRIO, up 0.8%.
Oil prices continued to rise as the war with Iran appeared increasingly far from a resolution after US President Donald Trump announced a package of measures aimed at hurting Iran’s economy.
Vale jumped 2.6%, despite a decline in Chinese iron ore futures.

Steelmakers, however, remained under pressure amid expectations of a possible agreement between Canada and the US that could lead to lower US tariffs on Canadian steel, making Brazilian companies less competitive.
Banks struggled as bond yields moved higher on energy-driven inflation concerns.
Banco do Brasil fell 0.2%, Bradesco dropped 1.7% and Itaú lost 2.2%.

sum: Here at Zacks, we focus on our proven ranking system, which places an emphasis on earnings estimates and estimate revisions, to find winning stocks. But we also understand that investors develop their own strategies, so we are constantly looking at the latest trends in value, growth, and momentum to find strong companies for our readers.

Considering these trends, value investing is clearly one of the most preferred ways to find strong stocks in any type of market. Value investors use tried-and-true metrics and fundamental analysis to find companies that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

In addition to the Zacks Rank, investors looking for stocks with specific traits can utilize our Style Scores system. Of course, value investors will be most interested in the system's "Value" category. Stocks with "A" grades for Value and high Zacks Ranks are among the best value stocks available at any given moment.

Investors should also recognize that BBDC has a P/B ratio of 0.83. The P/B is a method of comparing a stock's market value to its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. This stock's P/B looks attractive against its industry's average P/B of 0.85. Over the past 12 months, BBDC's P/B has been as high as 0.96 and as low as 0.70, with a median of 0.85.

Finally, our model also underscores that BBDC has a P/CF ratio of 10.55. This data point considers a firm's operating cash flow and is frequently used to find companies that are undervalued when considering their solid cash outlook. BBDC's P/CF compares to its industry's average P/CF of 11.30. Over the past year, BBDC's P/CF has been as high as 11.34 and as low as 9.09, with a median of 10.21.
Value investors will likely look at more than just these metrics, but the above data helps show that Barings BDC is likely undervalued currently.
